# Formula Reference Sheets {#sec-formula-sheet}

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Formulas are **conditional approximations**, not universal rules. The analytical method, sampling design and rounding convention must be justified before use.
:::

| Planning aim | Formula or relationship | Important qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Single proportion precision | $n_0=Z^2p(1-p)/d^2$ | Normal approximation; independent observations |
| Single mean precision | $n_0=Z^2\sigma^2/d^2$ | Anticipated SD and precision share units |
| Recruitment allowance | $n_{recruit}=\lceil n_{complete}/(1-L)\rceil$ | Explicit convention; does not correct attrition bias |
| Finite-population approximation | $n_{FPC}=n_0/[1+(n_0-1)/N]$ | Specified finite population and applicable sampling design |
| Equal-size cluster DEFF | $1+(m-1)\rho$ | Approximation; equal clusters, compatible estimand |
| Taro Yamane | $n=N/(1+Ne^2)$ | Simplified survey expression with restrictive conditions |
| Two independent means, balanced | $2\sigma^2(Z_{1-\alpha/2}+Z_{1-\beta})^2/\Delta^2$ per group | Common SD, normal approximation |
| RR-based second-group risk | $p_2=RR\,p_1$ | Valid probability and consistent event definition |
| OR-based second-group risk | $p_2=OR\,p_1/(1-p_1+OR\,p_1)$ | OR is not usually equal to RR |
| Pooled reference SD | $s_p=\sqrt{[(n_1-1)s_1^2+(n_2-1)s_2^2]/(n_1+n_2-2)}$ | Assumes common within-group variance |
| Diagnostic sensitivity precision | $n_D\approx Z^2Se(1-Se)/d^2$ | Diseased participants; Wald approximate planning |
| Diagnostic specificity precision | $n_{ND}\approx Z^2Sp(1-Sp)/d^2$ | Non-diseased participants; Wald approximate planning |

## Reporting checklist

For each calculation record: primary outcome and time point; objective; estimand; unit of measurement; design and sampling method; sources for parameters; formula or software method; assumptions; confidence or alpha/power; margins; allocation; design adjustments; recruitment allowance; rounding; complete and recruitable sample sizes.

For comparisons, a fully specified test and variance convention are necessary; there is no single universal two-proportion or two-mean formula. See [@consort2025; @cook2018].
